course.yaml:401 and brief:6 set one goal: construct a factored FFT while accounting for arithmetic, storage, ordering, and scaling. Every top-level section advances that construction or its consumer-facing choice; no independent topic is introduced.

The lesson has 4,461 whitespace-delimited words, five content sections, two derivations, two theorems, two body example-problem pairs, one lab, six closing exercises, and explicit boundary/implementation cases. It is at least as substantial as the gold chapter rather than a result summary.

The radix-2 theorem states N=2^m and the declared ledger at 228-240; the composite theorem states N=RM with R,M>1 and the output-index mapping at 334-346. Both proofs perform the claimed algebra/count. The definitions at 99-103 and 302-306 give operational membership clauses rather than decorative labels.

rubric_scores.criterion: Exercises produce DSP work and include parallel practice
rubric_scores.evidence: Closing exercises require schedule construction and numerical verification (443-459), boundary analysis (462-469), error diagnosis (472-479), benchmark design (482-491), strategy choice (494-505), and transfer to selected bins (508-531). Body pairs are near-isomorphic: zero-odd branch at 105-119 → zero-even branch at 121-148; safe butterfly at 170-184 → new values and overwrite diagnosis at 188-199.

The closed-book gate at 9-38 retrieves the DFT pair, sign/scale/order, even-odd split, circular convolution, and padding from the prerequisite. Closing exercise 3 cannot be solved without the inherited sign/scale/order contract (472-479), and exercise 6 requires the earlier zero-padding/bin-grid distinction (508-530). The set mixes construction, diagnosis, boundary, empirical design, and method selection without naming a uniform method.

Most solutions show full reasoning, but exercise 1 asks the learner to ‘Draw the radix-2 DIT schedule’ and verify all coefficients (443-444); its solution gives input order, counts, and the final array, then says only ‘The stage arrays are the three rows displayed in the storage section’ (447-458). It does not reproduce the schedule, butterfly pairings, or a direct-check path inside the solution.

rubric_scores.criterion: At most one mechanical closing exercise
rubric_scores.evidence: Exercise 1 at 443-459 is the sole warm-up/mechanical item and still combines drawing, counting, and numerical verification. Exercises 2-6 require boundary judgment, refutation, experimental design, strategy choice, or transfer.

Boundary probe: N=1, repeated factors, prime N at 462-469. False claim to refute: algorithm versus order/scale at 472-479. Research-shaped task: frozen benchmark protocol at 482-491. The set carries three of the four required types.

Only exercise 6 reaches forward: its solution says the eight coefficients are only evidence and explicitly Ref-links Phone-Channel DTMF Receiver at 530. Exercises 1-5 contain no forward Ref and close only current/prerequisite skills.

The FftCostGrowth caption at 242 already states ‘Structural operation counts predict different growth; they do not supply a universal wall-clock crossover.’ The immediately following KeyFact at 244-246 repeats the same asymptotic-count-versus-runtime claim and adds only a list of implementation constants already developed later. Deleting the box loses no distinct boundary or consequence. Other callouts pass: 150-152 binds correctness to restored interface contracts; 308-310 states the consumer-level consequence; 388-390 synthesizes radix and layout; 435-437 defines a publishable benchmark contract.

There are no survey-name interjections. Cooley and Tukey are named at 356 because the historical multiply-add unit itself is under discussion, so provenance changes how the count may be compared. The remaining source detail is confined to chapter/page-precise References at 534-539.

rubric_scores.criterion: No obvious narration or production-state prose

rubric_scores.criterion: Visuals are load-bearing and captions state claims
rubric_scores.evidence: The factorization sequence at 93 follows the exact N=8 computation and names reuse; the butterfly ledger at 186 follows the overwrite example; the cost figure at 242 follows the count theorem; the memory-order figure at 288 follows literal address/stage tables; the lab at 386 follows the N=960 budget derivation. Captions state reuse, safe overwrite, non-universal crossover, permutation restoration, and an achieved target rather than merely describing appearance.

rubric_scores.criterion: Demo makes consequential dynamic behavior visible
rubric_scores.evidence: The task at 382-384 asks the learner to repair an invalid factorization, cross T≤115,200, and restore order/scale until direct checks pass; the Demo at 386 provides those three observable targets. Its initial Power-of-two wall preset is nonblank and deliberately fails product 960, while named pass and fault presets permit guided diagnosis. This is not a slider-only duplicate of a static curve.

All five content sections are divided by ### subheads; prose runs are interrupted by equations, tables, typed environments, tasks, figures, or callouts before exceeding the three-paragraph norm. The longest derivation blocks at 201-246 and 318-390 have theorem/figure or theorem/task/demo breaks.

The skeleton reads: inherited split supplies two outputs → recursive butterflies replace quadratic repetition → in-place storage exposes order/scale → composite lengths factor → requested outputs select the computation. Captions add unchanged DFT, safe overwrite, count-versus-runtime, restored k order, and budget verification (93, 186, 242, 288, 386), so the throughline survives collapsed proofs/solutions.

Bold marks only the defined payoff token ‘FFT’ at 100; italics mark first-use ‘radix-2 butterfly’ at 168; inline code is used for the literal overwritten `a-t` expression at 197. Four em dashes across 4,461 words stay below the approximate density ceiling.

The mathematical prose is declarative and contains no rhetorical questions or exclamations, but the stale build-state clauses ‘When the sequence is built’ (96) and ‘In the planned lab’ (383) break the finished engineering register. The phrase ‘The displayed substitution is the proof’ (338) is apparatus narration rather than a proof-mode statement.
